chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from some of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Whoever kills a believer deliberately, he is subject to retaliation, unless the guardians of the killed one agree to accept the diya (blood money), or they mutually agree on more than the diya or less than the diya. If they do this among themselves, it is permissible, but if they retract, retaliation is applied.
And he said: The diya is ten thousand dirhams, or one thousand dinars, or one hundred camels.

key_terms.أَوْلِيَاء الْمَقْتُول: The guardians/heirs of the killed person who hold the right to demand qisas or accept diya
key_terms.الدِّيَة: Diya — blood money paid as compensation to the victim's family in lieu of qisas
key_terms.مُتَعَمِّداً: Deliberately — the intentional (amd) killing that triggers the qisas ruling
key_terms.يُقَادُ: Qisas (retaliation in kind) — the default legal penalty for intentional killing

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on intentional killing and blood money (diya) according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the Islamic ruling on intentional homicide: the default is qisas (equal retaliation), but the victim's heirs may choose to accept the diya (blood money) instead, or negotiate a different amount by mutual agreement. The Imam also specifies the three equivalent forms in which the diya may be paid. This ruling reflects the classical Shia jurisprudential position that the right of retaliation belongs to the heirs of the victim, not the state, with flexibility for settlement.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yunus, from one of our companions, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘The one who kills a Believer deliberately, so he would be retaliated with (the same), except if the guardians of the killed one happy with accepting the wergild, or if he makes them to be pleased with more than the wergild, or less than the wergild. So if he were to do that between them, it is allowed, and if they were to retract (from accepting the wergild), it would be retaliation’.
And he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The wergild is ten thousand Dirhams, or a thousand Dinars, or one hundred from the camels’.
